B6 water-gate disagreement: B6's sculk water-gate item rests on fluidState.is(Fluids.WATER) being true for flowing water; TypedInstance.is is a type-identity check (flowing water's type is FLOWING_WATER), so vanilla's gate is source-only and the port matches - B6's item may need withdrawal (evidence: b04/evidence/javap-TypedInstance-is.txt). test_brewing_parity.py:129 reads 26.3 resources where the 26.1 tree reads 26.1's - latent driver defect, moot while B4-O04 blocks the driver.
systemic_note: The 26.1.1 tree REGRESSED the 26.1 fixes: it carries 26.3-form code in files where the 26.1 tree carries corrected forms (items.rs, brewing.rs, providers.rs, menu.rs, block_entity_nbt.rs, block_entity_item.rs, sign_edit.rs, composter.rs, level/sculk.rs, dispenser.rs, spawner.rs, trial_spawner.rs, lan_stations.rs, save.rs, recipe_book.rs, machines.rs - diffs in b04/evidence/diffs/). The mechanism is one pattern: component/tag reads for data that does not exist in 26.1.1 (cooking_fuel, brewing_fuel, villager_food, compostable, mob_visibility, sign_text_front/back, waxed components; sculk_growth_inhibitors, extendable_maps tags). Where the 26.1 tree replaced those reads with the 26.1-form source (hardcoded tables, tag checks, FuelValues), the 26.1.1 tree reads the absent component/tag and gets nothing. Consequence: two 1.21.7 majors that 26.1 had FIXED are back (G01 furnaces never light, G02 brewing stands never brew), and 8 new defects (G30-G37) appear in systems that were correct in 26.1. Vanilla 26.1.1 == vanilla 26.1 for every Batch 4 class (PORT-NOTES-26.1.1.md), so every difference is a port-side regression, not a vanilla change.
